attributes.affiliation_basis: UNKNOWN: AIS states an identity and no side, and nothing in it is authenticated
attributes.attribution: Data delivered by BarentsWatch (the credit its API terms require); the data are collected by the Norwegian Coastal Administration and licensed under the Norwegian Licence for Open Government Data (NLOD), as read on 2026-10-22 (fixtures/barentswatch_hais/spec/barentswatch_hais_terms.json)
attributes.barentswatch_samples_basis: readings taken from each sampled element, keyed by sample index: index k is Track.samples[k] and residual.data.points[source_index[k]]. speed_mps is speedOverGround converted from knots; speed_at_or_above_maximum marks the 102.2 kn floor; course_deg and true_heading_deg are degrees; rate_of_turn is verbatim (unit not established); null and AIS sentinels read as null; sentinel_fields and null_fields name the keys each element marked unknown
attributes.duplicate_instants_basis: groups of samples sharing one instant, every one kept: identical means the elements are equal key for key (a re-delivered report), otherwise the same instant is stated with different values and nothing here chooses between them
attributes.entity_id_basis: the MMSI rendered as nine digits under AIS, as the ais adapter writes it, so a decoded AIS message and a BarentsWatch track of one vessel give one entity_id
attributes.entity_type_basis: FACILITY: the ais adapter's MMSI rule, so one MMSI has one entity type across both adapters; a coast-station or aid-to-navigation MMSI (mmsi_category) is a FACILITY whatever it transmits, every other is a PLATFORM
attributes.kinematics_basis: the last sample's element: speedOverGround in knots converted to m/s, courseOverGround in degrees true; null and the AIS sentinels (102.3 kn; 360 deg and above) are unknown, never zero. trueHeading has no CDM field and is parked per sample
attributes.names_basis: the distinct non-null name and shipType values in file order, verbatim; a shipType of 0 is AIS 'not available' and is listed as stated
attributes.points_without_position_basis: file indices of elements whose latitude or longitude is null or the AIS 'not available' value; they have no Track sample and stay whole in residual.data.points
attributes.position_basis: the Track's last sample: the latest element stating a position
attributes.position_source_basis: ESTIMATED, as the ais adapter reads an AIS position that states no EPFD and no usable UTC second: a BarentsWatch track element states neither, and ESTIMATED understates rather than overstates the fix, which is the safe direction for this field
attributes.source_order_basis: the order of msgtime across the file as delivered: descending (the API's observed newest-first order), ascending, single-instant or unordered; the samples are ascending whatever it was
attributes.symbol_basis: derived from affiliation; the file states no symbol
attributes.unknown_keys_basis: keys outside the twelve the API is observed to write, preserved verbatim in residual.data.points and read for nothing
attributes.valid_from_basis: the instant of the earliest sample
attributes.valid_to_basis: the instant of the latest sample: the file holds nothing after it, which says nothing about the vessel after it

transformations: [*].mmsi: the integer MMSI is rendered as nine decimal digits for its AIS source id, as the ais adapter writes it, so one vessel has one entity_id across both adapters

[*]: the elements, delivered newest first, are re-ordered ascending by msgtime into Track samples (sort key: instant, then descending file index); the residual keeps file order and attributes.barentswatch_samples.source_index maps each sample to its element
[*].msgtime: the RFC 3339 instant is converted to UTC and re-rendered in the CDM's three-decimal Z form, truncating any sub-millisecond digits

[*].speedOverGround: a speed in knots becomes metres per second (x 1852/3600, rounded to 4 decimals as the ais adapter does) in attributes.barentswatch_samples.speed_mps and, for the last sample, Kinematics.speed_mps; null and the 102.3 sentinel become absent

completeness.completeness_basis: carried_samples counts the elements stating a usable position; a file is one requested window of the vessel's history under a limited retention period and the provider's filtering, so it is a fragment, and the API states no total

transformations: [*].mmsi: the integer MMSI is rendered as nine decimal digits for its AIS source id, as the ais adapter writes it, so one vessel has one entity_id across both adapters

[*]: the elements, delivered newest first, are re-ordered ascending by msgtime into Track samples (sort key: instant, then descending file index); the residual keeps file order and attributes.barentswatch_samples.source_index maps each sample to its element
[*].msgtime: the RFC 3339 instant is converted to UTC and re-rendered in the CDM's three-decimal Z form, truncating any sub-millisecond digits

payload.event_id_basis: the MMSI and the first and last sample instants
payload.event_type_basis: TRACK_UPDATE: one track file is one update of a history
payload.observed_at_basis: the msgtime of the latest sample, the instant the provider recorded for that report, converted to UTC
payload.received_at_basis: the injected clock; the file states no delivery instant
payload.severity_basis: INFO: a history file states no urgency; navigational status is carried per sample and no alert is derived from it
payload.validity_basis: no validity: the event is an instant, and the span is the Entity's valid_from and valid_to and the Track's samples
